sections.heading: What to do now
list: Estimate your MAGI household income for 2026 (not just your paychecks): net rental income, savings interest, and any net trading gains count. See Income counting. If it is $22,025 or less for a one-person household, you are inside the Medi-Cal limit ($1,836/month).
Apply to Medi-Cal (or Covered California) right now. Medi-Cal can be applied for at any time of year — not just during open enrollment. One application screens you for both programs. See Apply.

Count your monthly income against the $580 test. You do not need earned income. The rule accepts "an income from any source of at least $580 (before taxes) in any month" — rental income, interest and trading income all count. See Work rules.

Line up a fallback of 80 hours. If a month falls under $580, volunteering, community service, a work program, or half-time school in that month satisfies the rule. School can be combined with the other hours.

Check for an exemption. A qualifying disability, caregiving for a child 13 or younger or a disabled person, pregnancy, CalFresh or CalWORKs work-requirement compliance, veteran with a total disability, tribal membership, and high-unemployment-county residence can excuse you entirely.

sections.heading: What this site does and does not do
list: Every number on this site comes from a federal, state, or Covered California source and links to it.
Your own income figures, county of residence, age, disability status, and immigration history are facts I cannot see. The tables are built around the thresholds, not around assumptions about you.
Values that could not be confirmed from an official source are left blank and listed on the Flagged for Review page rather than estimated.
This is research, not legal, tax, or immigration advice. For your own case, ask your county Medi-Cal office (DHCS: find a county office) and a tax professional.
